BioGA: Bioinformatics Genetic Algorithm

Source: R/BioGA-package.R
BioGA-package.Rd

BioGA provides a genetic algorithm framework for analyzing and optimizing high throughput genomic data. All core functions are implemented in C++ for performance via Rcpp and RcppParallel, with an easy-to-use R interface.

Details

Two representations are supported. In "real" mode individuals are continuous expression profiles; in "binary" mode individuals are gene selection indicators and class labels are required. The workflow is:

  1. Initialization: initialize_population_cpp() — Creates an initial population, optionally guided by gene clusters.

  2. Fitness evaluation: evaluate_fitness_cpp() — Evaluates two minimised objectives (data fidelity and parsimony in "real" mode; predictive signal and sparsity in "binary" mode), computed in parallel.

  3. Selection: selection_cpp() — Selects parents using NSGA-II rank and crowding-distance tournament selection.

  4. Crossover: crossover_cpp() — Generates offspring via simulated binary crossover (SBX) in "real" mode or uniform crossover in "binary" mode.

  5. Mutation: mutation_cpp() — Applies adaptive Gaussian (or bit-flip) mutation with optional degree-based network damping.

  6. Replacement: replacement_cpp() — Admits the best offspring by NSGA-II environmental selection.

  7. Main loop: bioga_main_cpp() — Orchestrates the full pipeline; bioga() is the user-facing entry point.
